cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: the inverse standard normal at probability 0.908789
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as 1.3333347. The independently computed quantile is 1.33333467, which rounds to 1.333335 at 6 dp (the input probability is itself a 6-dp rounding of Phi(1.333333), which is why the answer is not exactly 1.333333)

cases.description: The 50th percentile of the standard normal is zero
cases.expected_note: Phi(0) = 0.5, so the inverse of 0.5 is exactly 0

cases.description: NORM.S.INV inverts NORM.S.DIST exactly, so a full round trip returns the original z
cases.expected_note: The two functions are documented as inverses of each other; feeding the unrounded CDF value straight back must recover z = 1.5 to well within 6 dp

cases.description: Probability 1 is outside the open domain (the quantile is unbounded there)
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #NUM! if probability <= 0 or probability >= 1

cases.description: A negative probability is outside the domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #NUM! if probability <= 0 or probability >= 1
